knobs.name: capture_twice

L2-1: the sysTester.DirListing event names P and no other file

knobs.mechanism: CAPTURE is sent twice in a row; two products are written where the test expects one

knobs.name: corrupt_first_product

L2-2: the two sysTester.Sha256 events of P1 are equal

knobs.mechanism: sysTester.CORRUPT_PRODUCT(P1) is inserted before the second DUMP_SHA256 of P1: the first two bytes of its picture record are overwritten on board, as an overwriting second capture would; the test removes its products at teardown

knobs.name: delete_before_downlink

L5-5:
sha256 of record/raw/files/

== hash in the first sysTester.Sha256 event
the two sysTester.Sha256 events are equal

knobs.mechanism: DELETE(P) is inserted before DOWNLINK(P): the product is removed on board, so nothing is delivered and the later DELETE names no stored product

knobs.name: delete_other

L2-4: event productManager.ProductDeleted count == 1 and names P1
the sysTester.DirListing event names P2 only
event productManager.ProductStored count == 1 and names P2

knobs.mechanism: DELETE(P1) is sent as DELETE(P2), the product hashed by the preceding DUMP_SHA256; the wrong product is removed

knobs.name: downlink_existing

L6-1: no CFDP transaction starts at the ground in the window

knobs.mechanism: DOWNLINK(Dp_missing.fxd) is sent with the name of the product the test captured (read from the preceding ProductWritten event); the product is sent

knobs.name: second_capture_dropped
knobs.mechanism: the second CAPTURE is sent as cmdDisp.CMD_NO_OP; no command is rejected
